params.body:
A resource reaches its model through `__get`, so the analysis knew none of their fields — about a
hundred findings, and this is the place where that matters most: **a typo in a resource is a silent
null in what a partner receives**, which is exactly the kind of fault nobody reports.

Twenty-two resources now carry `@mixin`, which is the annotation and the documentation in one: you
can read from the class which model it turns into JSON, instead of chasing the call site.

**Pointing them at their model closed two real gaps in the model annotations.**

`Vehicle::$primary_photo` and `$primary_stocklist_photo` had none. Both relations go through
`firstPhoto()`, so the generator could not read their type out of the method — while they are used
on the sheet, on the showroom slide and in the partner API. `firstPhoto()` now declares what it
returns, and the two are written down with the reason.

`Option::$option_value` and `$option_value_id` had none either, and that one is worth knowing: the
relation on `Vehicle` pulls the pivot columns in as ordinary columns
(`->select(['options.*', 'option_value_id', 'option_value'])`), so an option loaded through a
vehicle carries them **twice** — on the model and on the pivot. Both spellings appear in the code
and both work; now the annotation says so instead of leaving the next reader to guess which is real.

| | |
|---|---|
| findings | 1.825 → **1.623** |
| entries | 187 removed, **0 added** |

No new finding surfaced from the mixins themselves, which is the honest answer to "are the
resources full of typos": they are not. What they were, was unreadable to the analyser. 1.826 tests
green.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
params.title: The API resources say which model they wrap
